sections.heading: Ser and ir: the same forms!
sections.body: In the preterite, *ser* and *ir* are identical. Context tells you which: *Fui a México* (I went to Mexico) vs. *Fue un día increíble* (It was an amazing day).

sections.heading: Irregular stems
sections.body: Many common verbs have an irregular stem in the preterite and share special endings: *-e, -iste, -o, -imos, -ieron* — with **no accents**.

sections.heading: Details
sections.body:
- *Hacer*: *hizo* is spelled with *z* to keep the sound.
- Stems ending in *j* (*dij-, traj-*) drop the *i* in the *ellos* form: *dijeron, trajeron* (not "dijieron").
- *Dar* takes -er endings without accents: *di, diste, dio, dimos, dieron*.
- *Hay* (from the verb *haber*) in the preterite is *hubo* (there was / there were — an event): *Hubo un accidente.*
- In the preterite, *saber* often means "found out" (*Supe la noticia ayer* — I found out yesterday) and *no poder* means "didn't manage to" (*No pude ir* — I couldn't go).

examples: Fui a México el verano pasado.
I went to Mexico last summer.
Estuve en casa todo el día.
I was at home all day.
Tuve un problema con el carro.
I had a problem with the car.
No pude ir a la fiesta.
I couldn't go to the party.
What did you do on the weekend?
Where did you put the keys?
I put them on the table.
I found out the news yesterday.
My aunt and uncle came to visit us.
Le di un regalo a mi madre.
I gave my mother a gift.
Hubo un accidente en la calle.
There was an accident on the street.
We were in Lima for three days.
I tried to call you, but I couldn't.
